evidence.claim: FreqMark reports DiffusionDB-source quality PSNR31.20/SSIM0.854; its VAE reference31.22/0.879 misses our targets too.
evidence.locator: Table1 and Figure4 quality table; section5.2
limitations: Author results, different pipeline; not our reproduction.

evidence.claim: The inspected method uses a DINOv2 decoder and500 freshly generated images from DiffusionDB prompts, not our existing-image blind-DCT profile.
limitations: Cannot transfer numerical fidelity or detection to our native datasets.

evidence.claim: VINE-B reports40.51dB/0.9954/0.0029 and VINE-R37.34dB/0.9934/0.0063, contradicting blanket impossibility of the three quality values.
limitations: Author-reported means over10000 paired images, not every-image guarantees or our results.
assumptions: Reported values and metric definitions hold for the described benchmark.

evidence.claim: VINE adds trained encoder-decoder skips, fine-tunes generative components, uses a ConvNeXt neural detector and resolution scaling; it does not validate our fixed SD1.5/blind-DCT route.
limitations: Replacement/training/resource/scope review is required before adoption.

open_questions: Can bounded source-latent refinement meet native source targets with the frozen decoder?
Can a reconstructed latent carry a recoverable blind image-DCT watermark without breaking q/h stability?
If fixed-decoder preservation fails, what source-detail-preserving amendment remains compatible with the thesis questions?
